### 7.1 Value types (CS-TYPES8, CS-TYPES8-NEG, CS-WIDEN)

| Family | Edge values |
| --- | --- |
| string | "", ASCII mixed case A E c z, NFC U+00E9 and NFD e U+0301 as distinct values, U+E000, U+10000, U+1F600, quote, backslash, CR, LF, a 64 KiB text |
| integer | 0, 1, -1, 2^53-1, -(2^53-1) on every lane; 2^53+1, 2^59-1, -2^59 where the lane accepts them; values beyond the lane's range belong to CS-RANGE-OUT |
| decimal | 0.00, 16.50, 16.49, a 38-digit value, a negative value, the TDK1 key and canonical text round trip (CS-DECIMAL covers scale overflow) |
| number (binary64, approximate values only) | +0.0, -0.0, 0.1, 0.30000000000000004, 1.0000000000000002, 2^53 as a double, 5e-324, 2.2250738585072014e-308, 1.7976931348623157e308, -1.5, 3.0 (stays a number) |
| boolean | true, false |
| datetime | 0, a negative instant, 1700000000000.5 (fractional millisecond), the earliest and latest instant Triplex accepts |
| ref | same type, another type, an entity created in the same command |
| json | {"b":1,"a":2} (key order kept), nested arrays and objects, non-ASCII text, 1e300 |
| blob | descriptor with and without filename, size 0, a size above 2^32 |

CS-TYPES8-NEG (each rejected atomically): lone surrogate, NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity, non-canonical integer text ("01", "+1", "1.0", "-0"), integer outside the core integer type, invalid datetime, unparseable json, blob descriptor with a negative size.

CS-WIDEN: integer 9007199254740993 first (lanes that accept it), then in the same attribute or physical column a whole-number float, a text value through an untyped attribute, and for QLever an invalid typed literal through the raw wire; re-read the first value everywhere.

### 7.2 Numbers (CS-NUMERIC) and errors (CS-ERRORS)

Every example in sections 4.1 to 4.4 is a CS-NUMERIC case with that expected answer. CS-ERRORS has one case per ERROR_TABLE entry reachable from a read surface.

### 7.3 Fault points (CS-FAULT)

The expected outcome after a fault is chosen from the last transition with durable or engine-side evidence observed by the fault injector after the crash (the log file's records read back, the engine's committed transactions, the publication marker), never from the system's own claim. A transition the protocol declares but the receipt does not witness fails the case.

**qlever transitions.**

| Transition | Witness evidence |
| --- | --- |
| QT0-RECEIVED | broker request log entry |
| QT1-VALIDATED | group member accepted against staged state (broker trace) |
| QT2-LOGGED | COMMIT record present in the log file after restart (fsync completed); this is the irrevocable decision |
| QT3-APPLY-SENT | update operation sent (broker trace) |
| QT4-PUBLISHED | publication marker for the group's P visible in a query |
| QT5-VERIFIED | complete expected effects and absences checked (broker trace and independent query through three access paths) |
| QT6-ACKED | caller received the success receipt |

**qlever expected outcomes.**

| Fault after | Final state | Original caller | Retry with the same commandId | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QT0-RECEIVED or QT1-VALIDATED (no QT2 evidence) | the command is absent unless a later attempt commits it; it is never committed twice | typed failure or E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; never success | evaluated as a fresh command (commits at most once in total) | - |
| QT2-LOGGED (no QT4 evidence) | the group MUST be published by recovery with the position decided at QT2; it can never become absent | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN or E-COMMIT-PENDING; never success before publication | before publication: E-COMMIT-PENDING or E-REPAIRING; after publication: the original success receipt (same txId and position) | never show the group before publication; E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT3-APPLY-SENT (no QT4 evidence) | as QT2-LOGGED; partial permutation state must not be served: the lane fences and recovery re-applies or rebuilds | as QT2-LOGGED | as QT2-LOGGED | E-REPAIRING while fenced; after recovery all access paths agree |
| QT4-PUBLISHED (no QT5 evidence) | published; recovery completes verification before any new write | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN or success; success only if publication was established | the original success receipt once publication is established, else E-REPAIRING | may show the group; E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT5-VERIFIED failure (verification mismatch) | lane fenced; recovery republishes the logged state; final state equals O-REPLAY with the group present | no success until recovery establishes publication | E-REPAIRING until recovered, then the original success receipt | E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT5-VERIFIED (no QT6 evidence): lost ACK | published | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN | the original success receipt | show the group |

A success receipt is valid only if its timestamp is after the group's QT4-PUBLISHED evidence; a read by the same client issued after the success receipt sees the group (read-your-writes).

**xtdb transitions.**

| Transition | Witness evidence |
| --- | --- |
| XT0-RECEIVED | client trace |
| XT1-BEGIN-SENT | driver trace |
| XT2-ENGINE-COMMITTED | the transaction is committed in the engine after restart (operation marker row present at its position) |
| XT3-ACKED | caller received the success receipt |

**xtdb expected outcomes.**

| Fault after | Final state | Original caller | Retry with the same commandId | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XT0 or XT1 (no XT2 evidence) | absent unless a later attempt commits it; never committed twice | typed failure or E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; never success | evaluated as a fresh command | - |
| XT2-ENGINE-COMMITTED (no XT3 evidence): lost ACK | present exactly once at its position | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; resolution through EP-RESOLVE returns committed | E-COMMAND-COMMITTED carrying the original txId (or the original receipt) | show the transaction (publication is atomic with commit) |

A success receipt is valid only after XT2 evidence; read-your-writes holds for the same client.

Access paths verified after each fault: XTDB `_id` lookup and column-predicate scan; QLever subject, predicate-object and object scans; plus the repository, the native surface in every language of the engine and the raw recipe.

### 7.4 Entity suite (CS-ENTITY)

- Schema: at least three EntityTypes using all eight families, cardinality one and many, required, optional, unique, a ref with target type and a reverse ref; two releases (v2 adds an optional attribute and a constraint).
- Command stream: create; correction; card-many add and remove; future validTo crossing later; retraction; with enforcement off, equal duplicates (one value, two supports) and distinct-value conflicts and overlapping intervals; presence toggles (convention until the Q9 policy); two commits sharing one recorded instant; a second runtime with a lagging clock; one nested transaction with two positions; the v2 release.
- Cut catalog: every phase position, recorded instants between and at commits (including the decreasing one), valid instants at, before and after every boundary; frozen from the oracle's derived positions, checked against receipts.
- Operations at each cut: get; getMany with missing ids; find with equality, range, membership and ref predicates per family, include, order, limit and cursor continuation; timeline; at(basis) for current, past R, past V and both. Conflicts expect E-CONFLICTING-VALUES per C5.
- Modes: current, reopen, engine restart. Size: a hand-built core of at most 200 entities plus a seeded generated variant.

### 7.5 Raw recipes (CS-RAW-RECIPES, CS-RAW-MAPPED)

The raw-query guide documents physical names, scope selection, how to express current, as-of position, recorded-time and valid-instant reads, the conflict indicator and values(attribute), every exact channel, every mapped recipe (RG-* entries of `capability-matrix.md`) and every known limit. Query classes: RP-POINT, RP-RANGE, RP-ORDER-PAGE, RP-CROSS-FAMILY, RP-JOIN, RP-ANTIJOIN, RP-AGGREGATE, RP-BASIS, RP-DATASET, RP-HISTORY, RP-INTERVAL, RP-JOURNAL.

### 7.6 Cursor and basis continuation (CS-CURSOR)

A cursor or a requested historical basis issued before any transition below continues successfully afterward (through the exact ledger path where the projection changed), returning exactly the rows O-REPLAY computes at the cursor's basis. An available retained cut never becomes unavailable because its projection, mapping or index changed. No retention policy exists, so 'cut no longer retained' is never a permitted outcome.

| Must continue | Transition |
| --- | --- |
| CT-ENGINE-RESTART | engine restart |
| CT-CLIENT-REOPEN | fresh runtime and client on the same scope |
| CT-RELEASE-CHANGE | a new schema release is published; the cursor continues under its own release's mapping |
| CT-PROJECTION-REBUILD | projection rebuilt or backfilled |
| CT-GENERATION-SWITCH | projection or index generation switch |
| CT-PUBLICATION-ADVANCE | newer commits published after the cursor's P |
| CT-MAINTAINING | QLever marker in MAINTAINING |
| CT-BOUNDARY-PASS | a valid-time boundary passes after the cursor was issued |
| CT-COMPACTION | XTDB compaction or GC, QLever rebuild-index or checkpoint |
| CT-BROKER-FAILOVER | broker replaced and recovery completed |
| CT-BACKUP-RESTORE | restore into a fresh engine from a backup taken after the cursor was issued |
| CT-FENCE-RECOVERED | lane fenced, then recovered: during the fence E-REPAIRING is permitted; after recovery the same cursor must continue |

| Permitted error case | Error | Reason | Only when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CE-MALFORMED | E-CURSOR | malformed | the token was altered or is not a token |
| CE-OTHER-SCOPE | E-CURSOR | other-scope | the cursor belongs to another scope |
| CE-OTHER-QUERY | E-CURSOR | other-query | the cursor belongs to a query with a different definition hash |
| CE-FUTURE-BASIS | E-UNAVAILABLE-CUT | unavailable-cut | the requested position is beyond the latest committed position |
| CE-FENCED | E-REPAIRING | repairing | only while the lane is fenced; the case also asserts continuation after recovery |

## 8. North-star workload, golden scenarios, year-one population and budgets

### 8.1 Fixed writer trace (TARGETS section 2)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Command shape | 5 to 10 facts: 0.6; 11 to 25 facts: 0.3; 26 to 50 facts: 0.1; one subject per command; blob reference for documents |
| Writers | people 0.4 (evidence, decisions); systems 0.3 (signals, often duplicated); agents 0.1 (proposals); runtime 0.2 (action outcomes) |
| Rate | steady 15 facts/s; bursts 750 facts/s for 60 s every 600 s |
| Duplicates | 0.1 of system signals re-sent with the same commandId |
| Lost ACKs | 0.01 of commands, retried |
| Corrections | 0.01 of commands, valid time 30 days back |
| Reads per write | 10 to 100: each command triggers a reconcile pull at the returned tx, dependency lookups, projection updates and UI refreshes |
| Conflicts | optimistic compare-and-set on the subject's last position; serial per subject, parallel across subjects |
| Bulk lane | separate and throttled; used only by the bulk measurements |
| Seed | a recorded seed fixes the whole trace; the same seed gives the same bytes |

The P1 reader ladder, the P2 to P4 probes, the P5 sweep and the secondary measurements are in `load-contract.json`.

### 8.2 Golden scenario rules (TARGETS section 6)

- A seeded, deterministic generator produces the command stream and the reads; the same seed gives the same bytes.
- Expected answers come from the independent oracles, never from a system under test: O-REPLAY for database state and values, O-DOMAIN for domain outputs and effects under WORLD_W0, or a frozen hand derivation with a citation (O-HAND).
- A scenario's commands are overlaid on the background trace, never instead of it; the receipt accounts for both streams separately.
- Every scenario carries positive witnesses (subjects that must change, GS-nn-WITNESS-POS) and negative witnesses (subjects that must not, GS-nn-WITNESS-NEG).
- Plan-impact preview (GS.11) and activation (GS.10) are compared at one common input basis (GS-10-11-COMMON-BASIS).
- The added failure schedules of GS_FAILURE_SCHEDULES (TARGETS 6.1) are named cases of their scenario and must meet their expected outcome.
- Each GS obligation binds only its own scenario: it selects its own tag and named cases, names exactly its own bars plus T-RUNS, and its receipt carries an ns-run whose measurement is its own scenario id (RULINGS Q26).
- Unless a scenario says otherwise it runs on P-YEAR-ONE with the fixed writer trace running and 256 concurrent pinned readers (P-NS).
- A scenario fails on any wrong answer, any lost or duplicated commit, any feed gap or order violation, or any missed bar; its receipt records the correctness verdicts and the P1 to P5 measurements together.
- All 20 run on every composition being compared, and the final acceptance reruns all 20 fresh.
- Numbers inside the scenarios: pay rates, hours and money use integer cents (the integer kind) or the decimal kind (TDK1 key); the scenarios include the range rules 'pay rate at or above 16.50' and 'hours over 40' (cases GS-NUM-RANGE-1650 and GS-NUM-HOURS-40, selected by GS.18's dashboard filters) and at least one write of a value the lane cannot hold, which must fail with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE, E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW or E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (GS-NUM-UNHOLDABLE, selected by GS.02).

### 8.3 Year-one measurement population

Role: measurement size for P1 to P5 and the golden scenarios; not a target in itself (lab/SCOPE.md section 2 item 2). Source: lab/TARGETS.md section 2 (year-one scale; rungs 10k, 100k, 1m, 10m) and section 1 P4 (history depths 1, 3, 10); qualification/benchmark-contract.json (topologies, query families); acceptance review r1 finding 13. Rungs: 10000, 100000, 1000000, 10000000; every count and stratum scales proportionally with the rung; hub in-degree is 1% of the rung's entities; shares are identical at every rung. At year one: {"entities": 10000000, "activeDomainFacts": 100000000, "retainedFactsMin": 150000000, "retainedFactsNote": "TARGETS section 2: retained history 150M to 500M facts per year; the history strata below give about 162M retained facts"}. Facts per entity: 10 active domain facts: label (string), risk score (number, approximate), pay rate (decimal, scale 2), hours (integer), headcount (integer), flag (boolean), group (ref), category (string, skewed), start date (datetime), status changed at (datetime). Written through public writes (EP-WRITER, or EP-BULK for the initial load), every command ACKed with a receipt, no unresolved outcome.

| Stratum | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| TN-LARGE | one tenant with 1m entities |
| TN-SMALL | 1,000 tenants with 1k entities each |
| TN-REST | the remaining entities in one default tenant |
| H1 | 0.5: depth 1: no correction |
| H3 | 0.35: depth 3: two corrections on each of five attributes |
| H10 | 0.15: depth 10: nine corrections on each of two attributes |
| EV-PRESENCE | 1 entity per 1,000 toggles presence true -> false -> true |
| EV-RETRO | 1% of commands are valid-time corrections 30 days back (TARGETS section 2) |
| EV-VALID-FUTURE | 5% of entities hold a fact whose validTo falls inside the measurement window |
| EV-VALID-PAST | 5% of entities hold a fact already closed by valid time |
| EV-SAME-R | 1 command per 10,000 shares its recorded instant with the next command |
| EV-DECREASING-R | 1 command per 10,000 is written by a second runtime whose clock is behind |
| EV-NESTED | 1 command per 10,000 is a nested transaction holding two positions |
| EV-UNHOLDABLE | write attempts of values a lane cannot hold (integers beyond its declared range, decimals beyond scale) appear in the stream and must fail typed |
| TP-CHAIN | 1,000 chains of depth 50 (at 10m; proportional below) |
| TP-TREE | 1,000 trees, fanout 4, depth 6 |
| TP-DIAMOND | 10,000 diamonds |
| TP-CYCLE | 1,000 cycles of length 3 to 20 |
| TP-FANOUT | 10 hubs, each with incoming refs from 1% of entities |
| TP-SKEW | category Zipf s = 1.1 over 1,000 values; flag about 50% true |
| TP-PULL | every subject's pull subgraph spans 3 to 6 hops and 50 to 2,000 facts (TARGETS P4) |
| RC-S | exactly 1 row |
| RC-M | 100 to 1,000 rows |
| RC-L | at least 100,000 rows or the documented row limit (E-ROW-LIMIT beyond) |

Counted separately: entities per tenant, domain facts, structural facts, assertion versions and retirements, config facts, journal, claim, receipt and feed metadata, maintenance relations, engine rows or triples by physical role, edges, presence events, corrections.

Correctness: S.correctness.query-families runs per rung, at least T-SAMPLES-PER-FAMILY samples per family with at least T-SAMPLES-PER-STRATUM in every applicable stratum (history, topology, tenant, result cardinality), plus complete-count queries for every population; deterministic sample selection from the generator seed, never from query answers.

### 8.4 Trace generator and offer schedule (TARGETS 2.1)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| source | lab/TARGETS.md section 2.1 (frozen before any comparison) |
| activeSet | {"share": 0.02, "examples": "200 subjects at the 10k rung, 200k at 10m", "residencyS": 2000, "replacement": "seeded draws"} |
| subjectChoice | {"fromActiveSet": 0.95, "activeSetDistribution": "Zipf s = 1.1 over a seeded ranking", "uniformAllSubjects": 0.05, "uniformWhy": "corrections and late signals"} |
| commandSize | uniform within each band of the 60/30/10 mix |
| offers | open loop: a seeded Poisson process at the steady rate |
| burstPhase | bursts start at 120 s + k x 600 s from the start of the measured window, identical for baselines and candidates |
| scenarioOverlay | a golden scenario's commands are added on top of the background trace, never instead of it; both streams accounted separately in the receipt |
| freeze | the generator source hash and the seed are bound in every receipt; a change to either starts a new comparison series |
| invalidCommands | {"share": 0.001, "rule": "0.1% of trace commands are deliberately invalid (values no engine may hold) and marked in the frozen trace; only those may end in a typed rejection", "source": "RULINGS Q31a, Q32c"} |

Measurement semantics for P1 to P5 (TARGETS 1.1: hot set, split reads, maintenance per window, driver-recorded basis, open-loop size bands, feed milestones and crash points, frozen pull buckets, the real release sweep) are in `load-contract.json` `measurements`.

### 8.5 World definition W0 and added failure schedules (TARGETS 6.1)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| role | a small frozen synthetic world definition used by every scenario, the P5 sweep and the P3 dependency rules; it stands in for Onboarded's real world definition and is not a Triplex product feature |
| rules | I-9 Section 1 task with a due time; I-9 Section 2 task with a due time; E-Verify status; background-check result; document expiry (valid-time boundaries); pay rate at or above the work location's minimum wage (a shared referenced entity); hours over 40 (overtime); start-date boundaries; proposals never count as decisions |
| ruleCount | about 12 |
| releases | two releases R1 and R2; R2 changes three requirements; releases are content-addressed and activation is a fact |
| implementations | the TypeScript reference kernel the drivers call, and O-DOMAIN, an independent stdlib-only Python oracle giving expected next tasks, obligations with due times, work items and effect traces from the same command stream |
| previewActivation | plan-impact preview (GS.11) and activation (GS.10) are compared at one common input basis (GS-10-11-COMMON-BASIS), never at different bases |
| witnesses | every scenario carries positive witnesses (subjects that must change) and negative witnesses (subjects that must not) |
| workItemIdentity | a work item's id is SHA-256 over canonical JSON of (subject, rule, kind, key) only; its content version hashes (release hash, input positions, payload) and is not the delivery identity; each id carries a durable publication sequence that increments whenever the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, and the outbox delivery key is (id, publication sequence); an activation that leaves the payload equal to the latest published one publishes nothing (early cutoff); duplicate-effect checks count by delivery key (RULINGS Q36a, Q38f) |
| affectedSet | the expected affected set of a transaction is the subjects whose static read set contains a changed fact; static read sets over-approximate and never miss (RULINGS Q36e) |
| version | W0-1.1.1, ACCEPTED at ada2e90 by V-D01's delta check and merged (e7c1346); its 95 file hashes are pinned (W0_PIN); the fingerprint pin waits for O-DOMAIN's reproduction (RULINGS Q40, Q44, Q48a) |
| nextEdit | W0-1.1.2 adds an R3 case with a listed jurisdiction that has no facts, adds "and A's entry for that rule is unscoped" to the SPEC 5.3 skip rule, and records measured R3 counts (9,497 reached, 418 changed) beside the expected ones; it changes no output, case result, floor or the fingerprint, and re-pinning its hashes needs a contract version bump (RULINGS Q48c) |
| ballast | rule-neutral ballast (owned answer entities <S>/ans:k with field and value text no rule reads, and a reference chain deep enough for 3 to 6 hops) sizes each world from P4's frozen buckets (50% 50-200 facts, 35% 201-800, 15% 801-2,000; a world may fall up to 2 facts below its bucket); trace commands use W0 and ballast attributes only, other attributes stay E_UNKNOWN; a ballast write affects nobody (RULINGS Q40a, Q44a) |
| twoHopFloor | the wage floor is S.location -> L.jurisdiction -> J.stateMinWageCents (R2's local floor stays on L), so the dependency index follows two references; cases: a jurisdiction wage write, re-pointing (L, jurisdiction), and the R1/R2 split at that depth (RULINGS Q40b) |
| positionOrdinal | positions in W0 are the 1-based dense ordinal of committed Triplex transacts in the tenant's source-of-truth stream, in coordinate order, supplied identically to the kernel and to O-DOMAIN (RULINGS Q40f) |
| generator | every draw field is named (including the passport expiry draw); the population fingerprint is pinned once O-DOMAIN's independent generator reproduces V-D01's, using SPEC 12.7's exact recipe (RULINGS Q40g, Q44a) |
| releaseR3 | R3 is a scoped release: OT threshold 2,700 minutes only for placements whose location's jurisdiction is in a listed set (about 10% of jurisdictions), reached through the reverse two-hop dependency index; the scope is part of the release's content hash; expected affected subjects and changed subjects are stated separately; plus a runtime-outcome attribute and population facts with later valid-from dates (RULINGS Q40i, Q44b) |
| misreadingCases | every case V-D01 lists as must-add and should-add is in W0's case set (RULINGS Q40e, Q44a) |
| fanout | work-location fanout is a seeded Zipf with s = 0.5 over 2,000 locations at the 100k rung (largest location about 1,100 workers, mean 50); other rungs keep N / 50 locations with the same s; only the 100k numbers are frozen floors (RULINGS Q36g, Q36h) |

| Scenario | Case | Added schedule | Expected outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GS.03 | GS-03-SUPERSEDED-REVISION | a vendor's older revision of a status arrives after a newer one for the same subject | acknowledged as superseded: no change to current values, recorded in the journal (provisional, flagged for Sam) |
| GS.04 | GS-04B-INDEX-PARTITION | the current index's feed consumer is cut for 60 s while the source keeps committing | commits and ACKs continue throughout the outage; on every serving surface the composition claims, native included, reads for which the index is not eligible wait at most 10 ms (COMPOSITION watermarkRouting) then route to the fallback; none answers from the stale index; the receipt measures the fallback share per window and the recovery time until the index is eligible again (RULINGS Q31e) |
| GS.06 | GS-06B-SHARED-REFERENCE | a work location's minimum wage changes (one shared referenced entity) | every worker at that location appears in the feed's affected-subject set and is re-run; no other worker is |
| GS.15 | GS-15-STORAGE-ACCESS | a tenant-A route attempts to read tenant B's storage directly | the access fails at the storage layer |
| GS.15 | GS-15-SLOW-TENANT | one tenant's feed consumer is slowed 10x | other tenants' feed lag and p99 hold |
| GS.19 | GS-19B-OUTBOX-CRASH | the consumer crashes after delivering an outbox item but before recording completion | the receiver deduplicates by the delivery key (id, publication sequence) of OUTBOX: exactly one externally visible effect per delivery key, and a later return to an earlier payload is a new delivery (RULINGS Q36a, Q38f) |

### 8.6 Budgets

Budgets are re-frozen after EXP-N02 measures the A0 controls, in a create-only budget-freeze receipt (A0 control measurements at every rung, this file's sha256), before any candidate is evaluated against them. No candidate comparison may cite a budget that has not been re-frozen. A hypothesis's predicted cost never sets its own allowance. Changing a budget creates a new profile version; loosening an NS bar needs Sam. A0 = the ledger-only baseline profile (status-quo adapters, no projection), measured on the same slot configuration, writer trace and rung. Where A0 cannot complete a rung, only the absolute bars and caps apply there and the failure is recorded. Every promotion and the final acceptance compare the integrated candidate with the frozen A0 control at the same rung, never with the previous promotion, so small regressions accumulate against one fixed reference. Every NS-* bar of obligations.json thresholds applies as an absolute budget at P-YEAR-ONE; resource caps: memory peak within the 11 GiB reservation pool, disk peak within the 50 GiB stop line of the 60 GiB VM (lab/PLAN.md section 8).

| Budget | Allowance vs A0 | Direction | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B-WRITE-BYTES-PER-FACT | 4.0 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16): projection, indexes, journal and feed together |
| B-INGEST-FACTS-PER-S | 0.5 | min | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |
| B-CURRENT-PULL-P99 | 1.0 | max | derived: the current path must not be slower than ledger-only |
| B-COMMIT-P99 | 1.25 | max | derived from NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256 |
| B-MEMORY-PEAK | 1.5 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |
| B-DISK-PEAK | 2.0 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |

Components counted: ledger, projection, index tables, journal, log of record, mutation broker, verification, scratch work, fallback (exact path) reads, maintenance, clients.

### 8.7 Composition identity (TARGETS 4.1, RULINGS Q28)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| assignments | source, current, history, analytics |
| engines | each assignment is XTDB or QLever |
| receiptBinding | every receipt binds, per assignment, the engine image digest, configuration hash and slot; every replication edge (feed consumer source hash, translation generation); and each serving index's watermark at read time |
| basis | a basis is a source-of-truth position (POSITION coordinates (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal)) plus a valid time |
| eligibility | index I is eligible to serve basis B only when all hold: its watermark (a fully resolved prefix) has reached B in B's epoch; C1's eligibility for the query (mapping, valid time, exact cut); I can actually reconstruct B (a current-only index only when B is at or after the last change to every attribute the read touches, the validity interval of R18); and I has applied every erasure published so far, independently of B (ERASURE frontier) (RULINGS Q31d) |
| watermarkRouting | a read that finds no eligible index waits at most T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS for one, then routes to an eligible fallback (the source of truth's own query surface or another index); the fallback's latency counts in the read's own latency; the receipt records the route and the surface language, a cross-language fallback is counted per surface, and fallbacks are reported as a share of reads per window; no index answers for a basis it is not eligible for (RULINGS Q31d) |
| fallbackEquivalence | outage read-your-own-write is tested on every serving surface the composition claims, native surfaces included; a stale fallback is rejected; where a fallback answers in another language, both recipes are bound to one semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and one expected answer from the oracle; total request latency and language attribution stay recorded (RULINGS Q34b) |
| ackOwnership | the source of truth sends the ACK after its own publication; read-your-own-write holds by routing (the pull at the returned position goes to an eligible index, else the fallback); in normal operation the current index is kept synchronous so the fast path serves that pull; during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue, pulls fall back, the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue, and fallback share and recovery time are measured (GS.04b); history and analytics stay asynchronous behind watermarks (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause) |
| layerSwaps | layers are swapped one at a time under matched workloads at small rungs (current-index candidates on P1 and P4; history candidates on past-basis reads and GS.12; source candidates on P2 and P3); only the two or three best compositions go on to end-to-end validation with the golden scenarios |
| scopeKey | an engine-scope receipt's key is (layer, the engine assigned to that layer, its image digest, configuration hash and slot), derived from the composition, never from engineOfLane |

### 8.8 Erasure (TARGETS section 7, RULINGS Q24)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| status | PROVISIONAL product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam: explain at a pre-erasure basis shows the marker, not the value |
| boundary | the boundary is the erasure commit's publication; a read that started before it may return, for each erased value, the old value or the marker (RULINGS Q49d); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value |
| shape | assertion identities and valid and record intervals keep their shape |
| reproduction | every reproduction contract holds modulo erasure: the C6 whole-journal comparison, raw and native query results, SDK results, cursor stability, bit-for-bit explain and GS.12; both sides of a comparison replace erased values with their markers before comparing (RULINGS Q31f) |
| frontier | an index or cache may serve any basis only after it has applied every erasure published so far, independently of the requested basis; an old-basis read never passes on the strength of its basis alone (RULINGS Q31f) |
| cacheInvalidation | erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry that holds the erased value |
| keyEvidence | for crypto-shredding, the lane's inventory shows that every surviving copy of a protected value, and of anything derived from it, is encrypted only under the destroyed key; deleting some key is not evidence |
| derivedChannels | a PII attribute's order key and lexical channel are inside the encrypted envelope (range rules on PII then run in the kernel after decryption), or the attribute is not eligible for range rules |
| restore | the erasure ledger is kept apart from the data and replayed after any restore or rebuild |
| journalCommit | an erasure commit is an ordinary data-journal transaction: it has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values; it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay; earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker, so ER-JOURNAL-MODULO compares markers on both sides (RULINGS Q49a) |
| idempotence | the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt; erasing it again changes nothing; an erase that matches nothing still commits, as a journal record with an empty change list (RULINGS Q49b) |
| queries | provisional, under the Q24 flag for Sam: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it; SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it; ORDER BY places erased markers last in a deterministic order by assertion id; grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker; Unique ignores erased values; an erased reference cannot be followed (an include returns the marker) (RULINGS Q49c) |
| inFlight | for a read that started before the erasure published, each erased value may be the old value or the marker (RULINGS Q49d) |
| tests | ER-PINNED-READER, ER-REBUILD, ER-RESTORE-PRE-BACKUP, ER-ORACLE-POST |

Protected-copy inventory, per lane: source log and journal, current index, history index, analytical copy, order-key channels, lexical channels, QLever broker log of record, caches, checkpoints, backups.

### 8.9 Evaluator counterexamples (RULINGS Q26)

Every obligation declares at least one mode. 'single-execution' runs each selected case once, so executions equal selections; NS and GS obligations use it explicitly (RULINGS Q26). Other modes (current, reopen, engine-restart) each run every selected case once more. A secondary threshold (RULINGS Q25) is measured and reported against its value every run; missing it never fails or blocks an obligation, and it never feeds a closure rule other than CR-METRICS.

| Id | Defeats | Receipt set | Why it stays OPEN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CX-CALIBRATION-EMPTY | CR-CALIBRATION | a VC record with an empty values list | an empty requirement set fails closed |
| CX-CALIBRATION-MISSING | CR-CALIBRATION, CR-NS | a VC record that omits one threshold an NS obligation names | every named threshold needs a record |
| CX-NS-MISSING-BAR | CR-NS | an ns-run with no measurement for one named bar | a missing bar is not a met bar |
| CX-NS-FEWER-RUNS | CR-NS, CR-GS | two independent runs where T-RUNS requires three | run count is part of the rule |
| CX-NS-ECHOED-BASIS | CR-NS | an ns-run whose reads carry only the engine-echoed basis, with no driver-recorded requested basis | answers are checked at the driver-recorded basis |

### 8.10 Position coordinates and gates (TARGETS 4.1, RULINGS Q31c, Q31i)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| coordinates | (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal): the source of truth's log stream and epoch, the engine's log offset (or the QLever broker's log frame) and the ordinal of a Triplex transact inside that engine transaction |
| order | lexicographic over (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal); positions need not be dense |
| nested | one engine transaction holding several Triplex transacts gives them consecutive ordinals at one offset, assigned atomically with the assertions and the subject compare-and-set |
| watermark | a fully resolved prefix: every position at or below it is applied or known aborted (stronger than the greatest position seen) |
| aborted | aborted offsets are accounted: the feed's resolution stream lists each one |
| epochs | a watermark from one epoch never satisfies a basis in another epoch without the mapping C1 defines |
| oracle | O-REPLAY treats positions as totally ordered coordinates: it sorts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts |
| falsifiers | FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION, FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP |
| falsifierText | {"FX-NESTED-CUTS": "cuts at every interior ordinal of one engine transaction holding several Triplex transacts", "FX-ABORT-GAP": "an aborted offset between two committed ones: cuts on both sides and the resolution-stream entry", "FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION": "a crash between appending a transaction and resolving it (applied or aborted)", "FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP": "a feed consumer resuming from a checkpoint that sits at an abort gap"} |

| Gate | Rule | Requires | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GATE-POSITION | no comparative or promotion claim on any composition, A0 included, until a VA-valid G7.position.coordinates receipt for that composition's source covers POSITION_REQUIRED_CASES, the four falsifiers included; no source-hash allowlist or declared density grants an exemption (RULINGS Q31c, Q38a; OUTSIDE_BLOCK_MUTATION_FIXTURE shows why) | G7.position.coordinates | NS.* and GS.* obligations and every comparative or promotion claim (CLAIM_ADMISSION) |
| GATE-W0 | no domain-dependent obligation closes until V-D01 has independently reviewed W0 (SPEC.md, releases, golden cases), every W0_PIN hash is pinned in this contract (RULINGS Q31i, Q48a) and O-DOMAIN has reproduced the population fingerprint (RULINGS Q40g); a null field fails closed | W0_PIN complete, W0.coverage-floors | every obligation whose oracles include O-DOMAIN |
| GATE-ORACLE-PIN | an obligation whose expected answers come from an oracle closes only once ORACLE_PINS pins that oracle's files with an acceptance receipt, the obligation is not in the pin's excludes, and the oracle does not refuse any case it selects (oracle_scope); a null pin fails closed (V-O02 C1, RULINGS Q45a, Q45b) | ORACLE_PINS complete for every oracle the obligation uses | every obligation using an oracle listed in ORACLE_PINS (O-REPLAY, O-TDK1) |
| GATE-TDK1-VECTORS | G1.decimal.tdk1-differential closes only once TDK1_VECTOR_PIN names a reviewed vector file by sha256; a null pin fails closed (RULINGS Q35, R20 V5) | TDK1_VECTOR_PIN complete | G1.decimal.tdk1-differential |

when any comparative or promotion claim is admitted, including one from a screening (P-SCREEN) receipt, the evaluator derives every prerequisite from validated, source-bound receipt evidence, never from supplied case names or Booleans: a VA-valid G7.position.coordinates receipt for the claim's own source tree and composition covering all of POSITION_REQUIRED_CASES; composition identity bound on every receipt (four assignments with image digest, configuration hash and slot); where any claimed obligation uses O-DOMAIN, the W0 pin and a W0.coverage-floors receipt; and a non-null, accepted ORACLE_PINS entry for every oracle the claim depends on, including the oracles of its prerequisite obligations, with the claimed obligation outside that pin's excludes and the oracle's refusals. Evidence is opened, never trusted by shape (RULINGS Q42a, Q47a): every referenced object exists in the content-addressed store and hashes to its recorded value, and every record matches its schema in EVIDENCE_SCHEMAS; the executed binary is bound to the claimed source tree through a build/import manifest object, and the binary and every executed or imported module it lists are retained objects whose bytes hash to the manifest; verifier records match the verifier-record schema; every case verdict is recomputed from its retained raw result, so an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED never counts as PASS, and the claim is rejected if any case the obligation selects, directly or through a broader case set, has a retained refusal (RULINGS Q47c); receipts are fresh (produced at the claim's commit, after the last change to any file in their dependency closure); modes, fault repetitions and verifier evidence are present; the claimed obligation's own measurement receipts exist with a matched control whose identity (commit, source tree, composition) comes from the frozen A0_REGISTRY entry for the claim's source engine, never from the claim, and whose nonempty, validated workload identity (WORKLOAD_IDENTITY: trace generator hash, seed, offer schedule hash, window, slot) equals the measurement's, a missing field never matching a missing field (RULINGS Q46b, Q47b); while the A0 registry entry is null every comparison is a diagnostic; unknown obligation ids are rejected, never dropped. lab/bin implements this (EXP-E01) with these functions as the reference model and adds the full VA rules (RULINGS Q41d). A claim with a failed or pending prerequisite is a diagnostic, never a qualified winner; while O-REPLAY's pin is null every claim is a diagnostic, and A0 measurements may run and produce diagnostics, never closures (RULINGS Q34d, Q37b, Q38b).


| Evidence record (RULINGS Q47a) | Fields | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| build-manifest/1 | schema, sourceTreeSha256, binarySha256, modules | binds the source tree to the executed binary; the binary and every executed or imported module ({path, sha256}, at least one) are retained objects whose bytes hash to the listed values |
| verifier-record/1 | schema, obligation, definitionSha256, verifier, verdict | names the receipt's obligation and definition hash, a nonempty verifier and the verdict ACCEPT |
| case-result/1 | schema, obligation, case, selection, oracle, oracleExit, oracleCode, expectedSha256, observedSha256 | the retained raw oracle run and observation for one case and the selection it covers; PASS only when oracleExit is 0, oracleCode is null, the expected and observed objects are both retained and equal; an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED is a refusal and never PASS (RULINGS Q45b, Q47a) |

Workload identity (RULINGS Q47b): every measurement and control receipt carries workload {generatorSourceSha256 (trace generator hash), seed, offerScheduleSha256, window [from, to] with 0 <= from < to, slot (the source assignment's slot)}, every field present, typed and nonempty; a control matches a measurement only when the two workload identities are equal field by field; a missing field never matches a missing field (RULINGS Q47b).


A0 registry (RULINGS Q46b, Q47b): when EXP-N01/N02 measures A0 at the budget re-freeze, the A0 commit, source tree and composition are frozen here in a contract version bump; the evaluator takes a comparison's control identity from the entry for the claim's source engine, never from the claim, so a candidate-selected control cannot qualify a comparison; while an entry is null every comparison against it is a diagnostic (RULINGS Q46b, Q47b). Entries: A0-XTDB null, fails closed; A0-QLEVER null, fails closed.


Pending rulings (RULINGS Q47d): RULINGS-PENDING.md may hold ruling rows; they carry no authority, are never compiled into this contract and never count as compiled RULINGS.md entries; the generator records the file's hash under inputs and lists the pending ids, and their presence never invalidates generation or --verify (RULINGS Q47d). ## 10. Obligations by section

### Goal 1. Exact value kinds, schemas, cardinality, uniqueness, references

**`G1.found.unchanged44`: Unchanged44 on the lane foundation.**
- Statement: The unchanged 44-case shared conformance suite (CS-U44) passes against the lane engine's Triples foundation in current and reopened form: 44 named cases per mode, zero skipped.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-U44 (all, EXISTS).
- Oracles: O-TESTKIT (EXISTS). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen; params {"gates": []}.
- Sources: wiki/goals.md:20-23; lab/research/R4-codebase-harness-map.md 5.3.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.value-kinds-roundtrip`: Every value kind in use round-trips exactly on every surface.**
- Statement: Every case of CS-TYPES8 (one assertion per value kind of VALUE_KINDS with the listed edge values, integers inside the lane's declared range) reads back exactly through Triples, the repository, the lane's native surface with a schema-derived contract, and the documented raw recipe, in current, reopen and engine-restart modes.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-TYPES8 (all, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-INTEGER-ROUND, M-NEGZERO.
- Sources: lab/SCOPE.md section 2 item 4; lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md section 5; lab/research/R2-qlever-capabilities.md 4.1.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.out-of-range-rejected`: Values a lane cannot hold fail with a typed error, never silently.**
- Statement: Every lane accepts every integer in [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]; on every qualified write route (the Triplex writer, the bulk import lane, replay and restore: RANGE-OUT-WRITER, RANGE-OUT-BULK, RANGE-OUT-REPLAY, RANGE-OUT-RESTORE) every CS-RANGE-OUT case (integers beyond the lane's declared LANE_INTEGER_RANGE, for QLever beyond +/-2^59) fails atomically with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any mutation, with no residue on any access path, and is never wrapped, widened or rounded. Bare native wire access is a diagnostic surface, not a qualified route: QLever's native wrap there is matrix row 51 (KNOWN-LIMIT KL-Q1) and diagnostic D-Q-INT60, never a failure of this obligation (RULINGS Q23).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-RANGE-OUT (all, TO-AUTHOR); CS-RANGE-OUT (RANGE-OUT-WRITER, RANGE-OUT-BULK, RANGE-OUT-REPLAY, RANGE-OUT-RESTORE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-RANGE-OUT (RANGE-OUT-RETRACT-PATTERN, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES, EP-WRITER, EP-BULK, EP-REPLAY. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen; params {"diagnostics": ["D-Q-INT60"], "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-OUT-OF-RANGE-WRAP.
- Sources: lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md section 5; lab/TARGETS.md section 3; lab/acceptance/RULINGS.md superseded section.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.decimal`: Decimal value kind for money and business decimals.**
- Statement: Every CS-DECIMAL case, per DECIMAL_RULES (RULINGS Q18) and the operation, conversion and scale tables DECIMAL_OPS, DECIMAL_CONVERSIONS and DECIMAL_SCALE_EVOLUTION (RULINGS Q22), one named case per row, plus DECIMAL_TESTS (adjacent large decimals, negatives, zero, scale boundaries, arithmetic intermediates, every query and serialization path, an independent order-key check, and input capture before normalization): each decimal attribute declares precision and scale; every precision is stored as the TDK1 key plus derived canonical text (RULINGS Q35b; the key bytes themselves are checked by G1.decimal.tdk1-admission and G1.decimal.tdk1-serialization under O-TDK1, RULINGS Q45c), compared exactly across attributes of different declared scale (DEC-CROSS-SCALE-COMPARE), and round-trips exactly on every surface; a decimal on an undeclared attribute (DEC-UNDECLARED-ATTRIBUTE) and -0.00 (DEC-NEGZERO-REFUSED) fail with E-INVALID-VALUE; 16.500 fits scale 2 and reads back as 16.50 (DEC-TRAILING-ZERO-FITS); toDecimal starts from the exact binary expansion (DEC-TODECIMAL-EXACT-EXPANSION); AVG over decimal fails with E-DECIMAL-AVG unless written with divide (DEC-AVG-PREFLIGHT) (RULINGS Q33b); every comparison with integer or number, equality included, is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY (DEC-CROSS-FAMILY-PREFLIGHT) and exact after explicit conversion (DEC-CONVERTED-COMPARE); results beyond the precision fail with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW, bare / with E-DECIMAL-BARE-DIVIDE, decimal to integer with a fraction with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION, and a narrowing migration that would lose digits with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING, atomically; range rules (for example 'pay rate at or above 16.50') compare in exact numeric order on the repository, fragments and documented raw channel; a value with more fractional digits than the scale fails with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (DEC-SCALE-EXCESS) and one outside the precision with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW (DEC-PRECISION-EXCESS), never rounded; kernel arithmetic over decimals is exact.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-DECIMAL (all, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-CROSS-SCALE-COMPARE, DEC-UNDECLARED-ATTRIBUTE, DEC-NEGZERO-REFUSED, DEC-TRAILING-ZERO-FITS, DEC-TODECIMAL-EXACT-EXPANSION, DEC-AVG-PREFLIGHT, DEC-SCALE-EXCESS, DEC-PRECISION-EXCESS, DEC-CROSS-FAMILY-PREFLIGHT, DEC-CONVERTED-COMPARE, DEC-OP-ADD, DEC-OP-MUL, DEC-OP-DIVIDE, DEC-OP-BARE-DIVIDE, DEC-OP-ROUND, DEC-OP-COMPARE, DEC-OP-SUM, DEC-CV-INT-TO-DEC, DEC-CV-DEC-TO-INT, DEC-CV-DEC-TO-NUM, DEC-CV-NUM-TO-DEC, DEC-CV-TEXT-TO-DEC, DEC-SCALE-WIDEN, DEC-SCALE-WIDEN-MIGRATE, DEC-SCALE-NARROW, DEC-ADJACENT-LARGE, DEC-NEGATIVE, DEC-ZERO, DEC-SCALE-BOUNDARY, DEC-INTERMEDIATE, DEC-EVERY-PATH, DEC-INPUT-CAPTURE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-WIRE-SHAPE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-OVERFLOW-IDS, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-LITERAL-TYPE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-ROUNDING-MODES, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-EXPR-LIMIT, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-ROUND-UP-SCALE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL (DEC-Q43-TOINTEGER-OVERFLOW, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES, EP-REPO, EP-WRITER, EP-KERNEL, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH, EP-FEED, EP-REPLAY. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.

**`G1.wire.write-guards`: Qualified write routes reject inexact JSON numbers and -0 instants.**
- Statement: Per WIRE_RULES WR-JSON, WR-INSTANT and WR-INTEGER-RANGE (RULINGS Q30a, Q30b, Q30e): on every qualified write route a JSON value holding -0, a non-finite number or an inexact binary64 at any depth, including inside List and Struct, fails atomically with E-INEXACT-JSON-NUMBER before CanonicalJson runs and before any mutation, where an inexact number is one that does not read back as written (Q33-JSON-READBACK, RULINGS Q33a); the guard applies to user JSON only, and the paired test holds on both engines: user JSON with -0 is rejected (WIRE-JSON-NEGZERO) while a number -0 assertion commits, journals, replays and reads back bit-exact (WIRE-JOURNAL-NUMBER-NEGZERO-ROUNDTRIP, RULINGS Q34c); an instant given as -0 fails with E-NEGATIVE-ZERO-INSTANT; the ProjectionSpec integer range rule covers only the safe-integer domain.

**`REQ.no-silent-precision-loss`: Requirement: No silent precision loss: exact storage and round trip for every value kind in use, order-preserving comparison for range-rule attributes, a hard error never silent conversion, integer range of at least 2^53, arithmetic over many rows only where a projection needs it.**
- Statement: No silent precision loss: exact storage and round trip for every value kind in use, order-preserving comparison for range-rule attributes, a hard error never silent conversion, integer range of at least 2^53, arithmetic over many rows only where a projection needs it. Each engine declares a route for this requirement, NATIVE or WORKAROUND (with its design id and a plain statement of what the engine cannot do natively); the requirement's own CS-REQ tests pass on that route. An open requirement never removes an engine from comparison. Starting points: XTDB: BIGINT, DECIMAL and VARCHAR store exactly; kernel arithmetic; split-sum only where a projection sums; QLever: lexical channels and fixed-width hex order keys; 60-bit integers cover 2^53; reject beyond +/-2^59 at write; kernel arithmetic.

### Goal 7. Atomic writes, receipts, migration and evolution, recovery

**`G7.outbox.publication-sequence`: Outbox deliveries are keyed by (id, publication sequence).**
- Statement: Per OUTBOX (RULINGS Q38f): the delivery key is (id, publication sequence); the sequence increments whenever the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, so a release rollback R1, R2, R1 publishes three deliveries 1650, 1700, 1650 (OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK); publication state is persisted atomically with its outbox record (OB-ATOMIC-STATE); a crash before delivery replays the same identity exactly once (OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY); an unchanged activation during recovery publishes nothing new while the pending delivery keeps its identity (OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY); a correction revert publishes a new sequence (OB-CORRECTION-REVERT); an older-basis evaluation publishes nothing (OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY, RULINGS Q40d); a retired id that reappears publishes a new sequence even with an unchanged payload (OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR, RULINGS Q40h); only live reconciles at the current basis are published (OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED, RULINGS Q44c).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-OUTBOX (all, TO-AUTHOR); CS-OUTBOX (OB-CORRECTION-REVERT, OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY, OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR, OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED, OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK, OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY, OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY, OB-ATOMIC-STATE, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-DOMAIN (TO-BUILD), O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-OUTBOX, EP-WRITER, EP-KERNEL. Profiles: P-FAULT.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-FAULT + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; thresholds T-FAULT-REPS; params {"gates": ["GATE-W0", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-OUTBOX-VERSION-DEDUP, M-OUTBOX-RETIREMENT-IGNORED.
- Sources: RULINGS Q38f; RULINGS Q40c; RULINGS Q40d; RULINGS Q40h; RULINGS Q44c; lab/reviews/plan-v2-round4.codex.md finding 8.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G7.composition.ack-and-routed-ryow`: ACK after source publication; read-your-own-write by routing.**
- Statement: Per COMPOSITION ackOwnership (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause): the source of truth sends every ACK after its own publication (CO-ACK-AFTER-SOURCE-PUBLICATION, OBS-ACK-ORDER); the pull at the returned position is served by an index eligible for it, else by the fallback, so read-your-own-write is exact (CO-RYOW-ROUTED); during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue and pulls fall back (CO-OUTAGE-ACKS-CONTINUE), and the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue (CO-CATCHUP-BOUNDED-QUEUE). Per COMPOSITION fallbackEquivalence (RULINGS Q34b), this holds on every serving surface the composition claims in the lane's language, native included (CO-RYOW-PER-SURFACE); a stale fallback is rejected (CO-STALE-FALLBACK-REJECTED); a cross-language fallback recipe is bound to the same semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and the same oracle answer (CO-CROSS-LANGUAGE-RECIPE-IDENTITY), with total request latency and language attribution recorded.

**`G7.position.coordinates`: Positions are totally ordered coordinates with a fully resolved watermark.**
- Statement: Per POSITION: a position is (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal), ordered lexicographically and not necessarily dense (PO-LEXICOGRAPHIC-ORDER); several Triplex transacts in one engine transaction take consecutive ordinals at one offset, assigned atomically with their assertions and the subject compare-and-set (PO-NESTED-CUTS-DENSE); a watermark is a fully resolved prefix and every aborted offset is listed in the feed's resolution stream (PO-ABORTED-LISTED); O-REPLAY sorts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts (PO-ORACLE-DENSE-ORDINALS). Every composition, A0 included, passes the four falsifiers FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION and FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP before any comparative or promotion claim (GATE-POSITION, RULINGS Q38a); a dense allocator passes them cheaply, and no allowlist exempts it (OUTSIDE_BLOCK_MUTATION_FIXTURE, mutant M-WITHTRANSACTION-REBIND).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-POSITION (PO-LEXICOGRAPHIC-ORDER, PO-ORACLE-DENSE-ORDINALS, PO-NESTED-CUTS-DENSE, FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION, FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP, PO-ABORTED-LISTED, TO-AUTHOR).

### Goal 9. Bitemporal intervals, presence, corrections, lineage, deletion, cascades

**`G9.erasure.visibility-boundary`: Erasure is a visibility boundary at the erasure commit's publication.**
- Statement: Every CS-ERASURE boundary, marker and reproduction case per ERASURE: a read that started before the erasure published may return, for each erased value, the old value or the marker (ER-INFLIGHT-READ, RULINGS Q49d); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value (ER-AFTER-PUBLICATION-ALL-BASES), with assertion identities and valid and record intervals unchanged (ER-SHAPE-KEPT); a reader already pinned when the erasure lands follows the same rule (ER-PINNED-READER); an index or cache serves any basis only after applying every published erasure, independently of the basis (ER-FRONTIER-OLD-BASIS), and erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry holding the value (ER-CACHE-INVALIDATION); expected post-erasure answers come independently from O-REPLAY (ER-ORACLE-POST).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (boundary, marker, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-INFLIGHT-READ, ER-AFTER-PUBLICATION-ALL-BASES, ER-SHAPE-KEPT, ER-PINNED-READER, ER-ORACLE-POST, ER-FRONTIER-OLD-BASIS, ER-CACHE-INVALIDATION, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-TRIPLES. Profiles: P-TINY-CONC.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-ERASURE-FRONTIER-SKIP.

**`G9.erasure.commit-semantics`: An erasure commit is an ordinary, idempotent journal transaction.**
- Statement: Per ERASURE journalCommit and idempotence (RULINGS Q49a, Q49b): an erasure commit has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values (ER-COMMIT-JOURNAL-IDENTITY-ONLY); it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay (ER-COMMIT-LEDGER); earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker (ER-EARLIER-CHANGE-MARKER); the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt and erasing it again changes nothing (ER-IDEMPOTENT-REERASE); an erase that matches nothing still commits a journal record with an empty change list (ER-EMPTY-ERASURE-RECORD).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (commit, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-COMMIT-JOURNAL-IDENTITY-ONLY, ER-COMMIT-LEDGER, ER-EARLIER-CHANGE-MARKER, ER-IDEMPOTENT-REERASE, ER-EMPTY-ERASURE-RECORD, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-TRIPLES, EP-REPLAY. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/TARGETS.md section 7 items 1 and 5; RULINGS Q24; RULINGS Q49a, Q49b.
- Notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G9.erasure.query-semantics`: Erased values give deterministic query answers.**
- Statement: Per ERASURE queries (RULINGS Q49c, provisional under the Q24 flag for Sam), on the repository, the native surface in the lane language and the raw recipes: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it (ER-PREDICATE-NO-MATCH); SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it (ER-AGGREGATE-SKIP-COUNT); ORDER BY places erased markers last, in a deterministic order by assertion id (ER-ORDER-MARKERS-LAST); grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker (ER-GROUP-ONE-MARKER); Unique ignores erased values (ER-UNIQUE-IGNORES); an erased reference cannot be followed and an include returns the marker (ER-REFERENCE-MARKER).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (queries, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-PREDICATE-NO-MATCH, ER-AGGREGATE-SKIP-COUNT, ER-ORDER-MARKERS-LAST, ER-GROUP-ONE-MARKER, ER-UNIQUE-IGNORES, ER-REFERENCE-MARKER, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.

### NS. North star: Sam's five priorities P1 to P5 on the fixed writer trace

**`NS.P1`: P1: many concurrent pinned reads that never block writers (per surface).**
- Statement: With the frozen writer trace running, closed-loop readers at 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256 (and 1,024 stress) each name their basis (valid time and record time or tx), in the lane's language, under TARGETS 1.1 P1: readers and writers share one hot set (at least half the reads target subjects written in the previous 60 s, NS-P1-HOT-SET); 10% of subgraph reads are split into two or more queries at the same named basis, scheduled to straddle a command the frozen trace already holds for that subject (step 1 before its ACK, step 2 after), and must equal the oracle at the requested basis (NS-P1-SPLIT-READ); the driver adds no writes of its own, so faster readers never change the write load (NS-P1-SPLIT-NO-DRIVER-WRITES, RULINGS Q31b); every window contains at least one maintenance event (NS-P1-MAINTENANCE-IN-WINDOW); the driver records the requested basis itself and the verifier checks answers at it (NS-P1-DRIVER-BASIS); reader-caused writer waits are attributed by matched-phase comparison against the zero-reader run and by engine-side wait evidence where the engine exposes it (NS-P1-WAIT-ATTRIBUTION). Every NS-P1-* bar holds: zero violations, goodput at 256 not below 64, read p99 within NS-P1-READ-P99-256-MS, writer commit p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256 of its zero-reader baseline, no command waits beyond NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS, and at 1,024 goodput within NS-P1-GOODPUT-1024-VS-256, writer p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-1024, back to the 256-level bar within NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: re-evaluate-and-spot.
- Cases: CS-NS (p1-ladder, p1-stress, COMPILED); CS-NS (NS-P1-HOT-SET, NS-P1-SPLIT-READ, NS-P1-SPLIT-NO-DRIVER-WRITES, NS-P1-MAINTENANCE-IN-WINDOW, NS-P1-DRIVER-BASIS, NS-P1-WAIT-ATTRIBUTION, COMPILED).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-OBS (TO-BUILD). Entrypoints: EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-WRITER, EP-ENGINE-OBS. Profiles: P-YEAR-ONE, P-NS.
- Closure: CR-NS; modes single-execution; thresholds NS-P1-VIOLATIONS-MAX, NS-P1-GOODPUT-256-VS-64, NS-P1-READ-P99-256-MS, NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256, NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS, NS-P1-GOODPUT-1024-VS-256, NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-1024, NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS, T-RUNS; params {"gates": ["GATE-POSITION", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/NORTH-STAR.md; lab/TARGETS.md sections 1 and 2.
- Status: OPEN.

**`NS.P2`: P2: small, atomic, idempotent per-subject commits with low latency.**
- Statement: Open loop under TARGETS 1.1 P2: commands are offered on the frozen schedule and latency runs from the scheduled offer to the published ACK (sent only once the commit is durable and readable), so queueing behind other writers counts. The trace's own commands are reported per size band: the 5-to-10 band (NS-P2-BAND-5-10) and the 11-to-25 band (NS-P2-BAND-11-25) each meet NS-P2-COMMIT-P50-MS and NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-MS, the 26-to-50 band (NS-P2-BAND-26-50) meets NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-26-50-MS, all with P1's 256 readers running; the 10-fact probe is a diagnostic only. Every offered command is committed with a receipt, rejected with a typed error, or a typed conflict (NS-P2-UNACCOUNTED-MAX, NS-P2-ACCOUNTING), and accounting is not progress: every oracle-valid trace command publishes; typed rejections count only for the trace's deliberately invalid commands and typed conflicts only where the oracle independently finds a compare-and-set race (NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX, NS-P2-PROGRESS); queued commands never exceed NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S of the offered rate at steady state (NS-P2-QUEUE-BOUND) and the queue drains within NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN-S after each burst (NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN) (RULINGS Q31a). The pull at the returned tx sees the commit every time with no extra wait (NS-P2-RYOW-FRACTION); duplicates and lost ACKs return the original receipt every time (NS-P2-DUP-RECEIPT-FRACTION).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: re-evaluate-and-spot.
- Cases: CS-NS (p2, COMPILED); CS-NS (NS-P2-BAND-5-10, NS-P2-BAND-11-25, NS-P2-BAND-26-50, NS-P2-ACCOUNTING, NS-P2-PROGRESS, NS-P2-QUEUE-BOUND, NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN, COMPILED).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-OBS (TO-BUILD). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-RESOLVE. Profiles: P-YEAR-ONE, P-NS.
- Closure: CR-NS; modes single-execution; thresholds NS-P2-COMMIT-P50-MS, NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-MS, NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-26-50-MS, NS-P2-UNACCOUNTED-MAX, NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX, NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S, NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN-S, NS-P2-RYOW-FRACTION, NS-P2-DUP-RECEIPT-FRACTION, T-RUNS; params {"gates": ["GATE-POSITION", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/NORTH-STAR.md; lab/TARGETS.md sections 1 and 2.
- Status: OPEN.

**`NS.P3`: P3: an ordered, resumable change feed.**
- Statement: Under TARGETS 1.1 P3: feed entries carry tx, entity, attribute and the valid-time range affected; commit time is the source's publication instant on the shared host monotonic clock; the cursor is (epoch, position); the expected affected-subject set per transaction is the directly written subjects (O-REPLAY) plus the subjects whose WORLD_W0 static read set contains a changed fact (O-DOMAIN, NS-P3-DOMAIN-AFFECTED-SET, RULINGS Q36e); 'affected subjects known' is the consumer's single durable write of the set and its checkpoint. Over a run there are zero gaps (NS-P3-GAPS-MAX) and zero per-subject order violations (NS-P3-ORDER-VIOLATIONS-MAX); lag stays within NS-P3-LAG-P99-MS with P1's 256 readers running; delivery is at-least-once from the last checkpoint with effects keyed by (consumer, position, subject), so crashes before the effect, after the effect before the checkpoint, and after the checkpoint (NS-P3-CRASH-BEFORE-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-CHECKPOINT) leave zero visible duplicate effects (NS-P3-VISIBLE-DUP-EFFECTS-MAX) while replay attempts are counted separately; resume from a checkpoint replays exactly.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: re-evaluate-and-spot.
- Cases: CS-NS (p3, COMPILED); CS-NS (NS-P3-CRASH-BEFORE-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-CHECKPOINT, NS-P3-DOMAIN-AFFECTED-SET, COMPILED).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-DOMAIN (TO-BUILD), O-OBS (TO-BUILD). Entrypoints: EP-FEED, EP-WRITER, EP-ENGINE-OBS. Profiles: P-YEAR-ONE, P-NS.
- Closure: CR-NS; modes single-execution; thresholds NS-P3-GAPS-MAX, NS-P3-ORDER-VIOLATIONS-MAX, NS-P3-LAG-P99-MS, NS-P3-VISIBLE-DUP-EFFECTS-MAX, T-RUNS; params {"gates": ["GATE-POSITION", "GATE-W0", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/NORTH-STAR.md; lab/TARGETS.md sections 1, 1.1 and 2.
- Status: OPEN.

**`NS.P4`: P4: a fast path to current values, separate from history (per surface).**
- Statement: Under TARGETS 1.1 P4: subject pulls at the current basis in the lane's language over the frozen weighted buckets (50% 50 to 200 facts, 35% 201 to 800, 15% 801 to 2,000; hops 3 at 40%, 4 at 35%, 6 at 25%; NS-P4-BUCKETS) meet NS-P4-PULL-P50-MS and NS-P4-PULL-P99-MS single-client on the weighted mix, each bucket reports its own p50 and p99, and the largest bucket meets NS-P4-PULL-P99-LARGEST-MS; throughput sustains NS-P4-PULLS-PER-CORE per engine core, with cores taken from the CPU quota bound in the receipt and host broker and kernel CPU reported beside it; on one matched sample of 1,000 subjects grown from history depth 1 to 3 to 10, current-pull p99 and bytes read stay within NS-P4-HISTORY-FLATNESS (NS-P4-MATCHED-HISTORY, RULINGS Q27); the receipt records whether current reads touch history.
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: re-evaluate-and-spot.
- Cases: CS-NS (p4, COMPILED); CS-NS (NS-P4-BUCKETS, NS-P4-MATCHED-HISTORY, COMPILED).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-OBS (TO-BUILD). Entrypoints: EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-ENGINE-OBS. Profiles: P-YEAR-ONE, P-NS.
- Closure: CR-NS; modes single-execution; thresholds NS-P4-PULL-P50-MS, NS-P4-PULL-P99-MS, NS-P4-PULL-P99-LARGEST-MS, NS-P4-PULLS-PER-CORE, NS-P4-HISTORY-FLATNESS, T-RUNS; params {"gates": ["GATE-POSITION", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/NORTH-STAR.md; lab/TARGETS.md sections 1 and 2.
- Status: OPEN.

**`NS.P5`: P5: release activation re-evaluates 100k subjects without hurting live traffic (per surface).**
- Statement: Under TARGETS 1.1 P5: a sweep evaluates release R against WORLD_W0 for every subject in R's scope at one shared basis, in the lane's language, while the writer trace and 64 live readers run; the receipt binds the basis and R's content hash; coverage is exact, every in-scope subject evaluated exactly once with the subject-list hash recorded (NS-P5-COVERAGE); a scoped release (W0 R3) is measured at the 100k rung, where its scope is not vacuous, and its receipt binds the reached-subject list and that list's hash instead of every placement (9,497 reached at 100k in V-D01's measurement; NS-P5-SCOPED-RELEASE-REACHED, RULINGS Q48b); results are published as work items through EP-OUTBOX under the delivery key (id, publication sequence) with early cutoff, so an activation that leaves a payload equal to the latest published one publishes nothing and a return to an earlier payload publishes a new sequence (RULINGS Q36a, Q38f), and equal O-DOMAIN's expected outputs; subjects the driver mutates after the basis is captured keep sweep outputs at the captured basis (NS-P5-POST-CAPTURE-MUTATION). Wall time including evaluation and publication stays within NS-P5-SWEEP-S; live read p99 and writer commit p99 stay within NS-P5-LIVE-READ-P99-RATIO and NS-P5-WRITER-P99-RATIO of their no-sweep values; a throttled variant of about 10 minutes overlaps a real compaction or index rebuild, keeps its basis and never blocks writers (no command waits beyond NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS; OBS-MAINTENANCE shows the maintenance completing; NS-P5-THROTTLED-COMPACTION).
- Lanes: all three; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: re-evaluate-and-spot.
- Cases: CS-NS (p5, COMPILED); CS-NS (NS-P5-COVERAGE, NS-P5-POST-CAPTURE-MUTATION, NS-P5-THROTTLED-COMPACTION, NS-P5-SCOPED-RELEASE-REACHED, COMPILED).

**`GS.04`: Lost acknowledgements and a restart (P2, P1).**

Added failure schedule GS-04B-INDEX-PARTITION: the current index's feed consumer is cut for 60 s while the source keeps committing; expected: commits and ACKs continue throughout the outage; on every serving surface the composition claims, native included, reads for which the index is not eligible wait at most 10 ms (COMPOSITION watermarkRouting) then route to the fallback; none answers from the stale index; the receipt measures the fallback share per window and the recovery time until the index is eligible again (RULINGS Q31e).
